newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasolines pause after two-day gain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasolines pause after two-day gain.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices paused mid-Wednesday after a two-day run-up, with most refineries back from spring maintenance and traders shrugging off rumors of operation problems at Unocal.
Traders said no major refineries were buying, with at least one offering to sell crude in San Francisco.
"I don't know if we'll continue to go up," one broker said, referring to the three-cent increase in CARB gasoline this week.
Traders dismissed rumors of unit shutdowns at Unocal's California plants, which are in the midst of layoffs.
Job cuts began early Tuesday, ahead of Tosco's March 31 acquistion of the refineries, said an official for the oil workers union.
Meawhile, some units at Exxon's Bay-area plant remained shut for planned maintenance, along with sections of two Unocal plants.

Meanwhile, the supply situation out west improved, with American Petroleum Institute (AP) reporting Tuesday that stocks of West Coast gasoline rose 861,000 barrels last week from an 11-year low of 25.6 million the week before.
Wholesale prices for conventional unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles remained 82/83 cents a gallon, while CARB gasoline held at Tuesday's 86/87-cent range.
Sellers came forward in the San Francisco gasoline market, hoping to take advantage of a two-cent profit as Bay grades rose to parity with L.A. amid Exxon's maintenance, traders said.
"If you could sell the Bay and buy L.A. at even, you make two cents," one broker said.
